utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... absolutely right. I understand your comment. But how do you know that this page we have on the screen now relates to the person we discussed?

This page doesn't say anything about [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... if I can help. Witness can maybe not see it Your Honour here on top of this page we can see ICRC ID, BAZ-100950-01 as the identification number and we go to the second page of the same document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see the name number [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I wished that the witness would have clearly answered that which is obvious for everyone. My main concern is is there any dispute about questions whether it's important to cross-reference information? Do the parties agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Absolutely agree on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Absolute. You as well. That's apparently what you wanted to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we want to establish that list is not correct and is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: Yes. But if I take you back to the previous one, you've shown us a document that someone died in a car accident. Apparently, you have not paid any attention to it, and I think you left that, at least I didn't hear any further questions about that. So that suggestion, I just wanted to let you know, that from a logical point of view, that if two documents are wrong, it still has to be established which one is wrong. The same is true here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly, and we want to say that those lists offered by Prosecution as the evidence, into evidence in our trial are not correct. Because they are not checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a mistake on that document and that's what we are trying to prove and we'll prove there is more. Of course.

utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm moving forward.

utterances.text: Before we proceed, sir, I would like to understand what all these documents mean. Are they giving us the final answer or are they part of a process of verifying the correct information? Could we please have a look at, for instance, at the ICRC documents, that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Sir, what does this document purport to do? Is it giving us information about what has happened or is it requesting information? Now, my understanding of that heading is they've got some information from somebody which they give here, the name of person and date of birth and what have you, and where the information says the person was -- was last seen or disappeared but it is requesting - I don't know to whom it is addressed - it's requesting further information about this person. utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it says up here that as an information request, request for information, or request for search. I have to give you a broader explanation. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is --

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many cases that we're going to look at today. The family has the right, on the basis of the Law on Missing person of Bosnia-Herzegovina, from the moment when the institute was established and according to previous laws we also had a three-year deadline and that is when persons could be declared missing. Having disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down because otherwise the interpreters would miss some of your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So a family member is allowed to go either to the place where the person had been born, in this case, I think, it's Srebrenica, or Bratunac, and in the municipal court of their new place of residence, a person can also be declared missing. We see that there are major deviations here within the family itself concerning the time of death and thereby the place and the circumstances involved. However, irregardless of that, all -- we did not complete the verification process. The municipal court issues, at the request of a family member and you see there are differences among the family members, the court issues a certificate of death on the basis of that, the place of birth of the missing person. On the basis of this decision, of the municipal court, this person is registered in the death register with the date that is recorded in the decision of the municipal court. So that date is questionable. I repeat once again: We were given the authority, we were supposed to be the ones who were supposed to do that. On the basis of which document this kind of thing is done, I really don't know. Now, irrespective of that -- well, it's -- it's a bit of a fait accompli, isn't it? We are supposed to observe the decision of the court regardless of how it was made, on the basis of a document that we are not certain of, we are not certain that the information contained in that document is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we first looked at -- in private session, about the conclusions in -- I think it was the ICMP report. There no one says that this person has died. This Chamber is mainly interested to see how these mistakes affect the reliability of the evidence presented by the Prosecution, and in this specific case, whatever a court said, you read to us the evidence as presented by the Prosecution, that is, this person is still missing, not that he's dead, not how he died, not that he is identified in any grave. utterances.text: My job is to show you the differences in between the documents and you can find it on page 10 of this document in regard of the [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand it your job to cast doubt - at least if you think doubt should be casted - on evidence presented by the Prosecution where the Prosecution wants us to draw certain conclusions. The question is whether this documentation can challenge a document presented by the evidence that the person is still missing. Please proceed. Especially because you say that this document - at least that is what the witness tell us - that it is unclear whether the certificate of death is a reliable source of information for the death of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Misic, who in Bosnia-Herzegovina has the authority to establish finally? Is it ICMP, is it ICRC, it your institute where you work? Who has the authority to establish that?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the Law on Missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we are the ones who are supposed to establish. Of course, in some cases, it is impossible to establish this exactly. However, what is impermissible is to make a difference or a distinction in terms of years and that is why certain documents, in our view, are lacking. What am I trying to say? During the war, for one and the same person, there is a document stated that he went missing in 1993 or in 1995 and then that is stated in 1997 and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I think you have you answered the question with your first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us briefly take a look at P1901. We're going back to the same document again. We need page 36 in that document. The English version will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And that should not be broadcast, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us briefly move into private session, please. This document should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 25. In 1D5388.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see this is a document from the International Committee of the Red Cross with the same name, surname, father's name, the date of birth is corrected. Originally it was the same date of birth as in the previous list. And then it's corrected to 28th August 1965 in longhand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 28th or 20th?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here in the document towards the bottom: "Approaching the deepest line of the front line, the group, including the above-said person, ran into a Bosnian Serb army group, and since then, there has been no news of him. [Interpretation] Here again we see the missing person file. It says the person went missing on 12 July 1995. [In English] One version would suffice. [Interpretation] On the list of missing persons of the ICMP, this person is indicated as having gone missing on 1st January 1993. Did you deal with this case, Mr. Misic?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, it's unclear how it's possible to make a report like this after the war in May 1996, when things were rather well-known. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know when people began making reports to the ICMP for identification?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as they began DNA analysis for purposes of identification. Then this data began to be collected, and people also provided descriptions of circumstances of disappearance and other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock. If you say one or two questions would do, then otherwise ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The comment says the old database of the ICMP. Gone missing on the route from Kladanj-Vlasenica in 1993 or 1994. In the ICRC book, the place of disappearance is Baljkovica, 12 July 1995. The father is no longer alive, one brother missing. A brother and two sisters reported the place of disappearance as Tuzla, 1994 or 1995. In the course of your work, did you compare this data?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this ICMP comment is the comment that the family usually provides when they give blood samples. And the information from the ICMP should be taken as the most relevant. It says here it was in 1993. Certainly not in 1994 or 1995, as in the next two reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 1993 and 1994, certainly not in 1995. That's what the witness said, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You speak too fast, and you are creating problems for the interpreters. Did you say that it could not have been in 1994 or in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The probability of that person disappearing in 1995 is very, very low. The most probable thing is that the family's comment is true, as recorded in the ICMP database.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for the break. We're actually overtime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, one short question. Why do you consider the information by the family probably truthful and the other information not? And do you know what the source of information for the ICRC was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the ICRC source was. We should ask them. It's usually the families. But this information recorded by the ICMP, it probably came later when the DNA analysis began in 1996. By that time, the families already had some information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But this is all assumptions. You don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, we are in the process of establishing that. We will establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Misic, we have no time to go through everything. We'll just look at the last one in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at P1901 first, without broadcasting it. Again, it's a document about the missing in Srebrenica. And in the English version, we need page 49. [In English] Can we go to a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, let's see once again 1D5388. And we need page 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, first of all, we see the name, the same number, BAZ-102629-01 same surname, same father's name, same date of birth. Below, it is stated under circumstances of disappearance that he went missing on the 11th or 12th July 1995, when the VRS took control of Srebrenica. The next page, the same number, same name, surname, father's name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... excuse me, I see under circumstances a different date of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're looking at this page that's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we looking at page -- can we go back one page, please. Can we go back one page, please. I was reading from this page. It's page 90 in this document. Can we enlarge only English version, please, the right one.

utterances.text: Yes, now this document is -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have it in paper [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: The problem if you refer to this [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.text: One second. Let's be careful. Were we reading from what page in the document?

utterances.text: We were reading from the page 90.

utterances.text: 90. Then ...

utterances.text: That's not page 90 in e-court. In e-court, it is page 89, and let's just have a look. We are now looking at 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, because that's the page number it has in e-court. I can't change that, so the why is -- and you, I think, presented this. Now, on page 90 - and perhaps we move to that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next one.

utterances.text: -- the next one is also about the same person.

utterances.text: -- concerned. Okay. So we first looked not at page 90 but 89 and now we are looking at page 90, which, as far as we can see, at first eye, is about the same person. And --

utterances.text: It's the same number, the same last name, the same name, the same father's name. The same date of birth. Only date and place of disappearance is 8th of December, 1992. Also the document issued by ICRC -- ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And these are documents from different dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One is from May 1996, that's page 89. 13th of May. And page 90, is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: February --

utterances.text: February 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: So apparently the information in February 1996 was different from the information or at least the basis on which they asked for further information in February 1996 was different from a similar document requesting further information as was made in May 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's where we are. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need the next page. If we check the top of the page, we would see the same number, identification number, which is BAZ-102629-01 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- no speaking aloud.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have B/C/S version on the left-hand side, please. Page 91 in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have the B/C/S. No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 91, please. You go two pages ahead. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Lukic, perhaps you clarify with the witness, this is section 2, information on disappearance. Now we have two previous pages for -- requests for further information. Is this an annex to which one or is it not an annex at all? It's section 2 of what kind of document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's part of a report. It's a so-called during life case file with information taken about the person, the status of the person, in the antemortem database and it's about the same person. It's something that will help with the final identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... who drafted this document, which is now on our screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person who filled in a report on a missing person. It should be a clerk of the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it stems from the ICRC, you're telling us. Could you tell us what date this has been drafted? Because we have two dates for requests for information, and I wonder whether this stems from February 1996 or May 1996 or any other date. Could you tell us when this was drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't tell you that because we can't see that from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we do not know from what time this document stems. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see from the document itself, on the right-hand side, the largest piece of text says he set out from Tuzla on 10 December 1992, together with a medical team, towards Srebrenica. So in this second document, Ruzina Voda is mentioned and the date and place of disappearance we see 12 December, 1992 at Ruzina Voda.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says 10 December.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in the previous document, it was 8 December. Now the next document comes from the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page in the same document, page 92; only in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that on the list of missing persons, under the same name and surname and father's name, the date of disappearance is 11 July 1995 in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the case file of the missing person at the Federal Commission for Missing Persons. We read here that this man, corresponding to the same information went missing on 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let's look at the next document, an excerpt from the register of deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The date, month, and year of death are recorded as 12 July 1995. Did you work on this case, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's questionable. You see this document from the register of deaths, it was issued in Srebrenica municipality, and it was drafted - look at the notes - it's a subsequent entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was made based on a final decision of the basic court.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read exactly but it is not in Srebrenica. It was probably entered at the place where the family filed the request to declare this person dead. So I stress the facts had not been established and the time and place and circumstances of his disappearance had not been established for a fact at the time when the judge issued this decision and a corresponding entry was made in the register of deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we should like to tender this document, to be marked for identification, because, at this moment, we don't have a complete translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you assign a number to start with, and then we'll hear from Mr. Jeremy whether there are any objections.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D1098 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would say firstly that the document relates to I think to 17 different people, only a few of which we've actually discussed in court so I would query the relevance of the additional -- of the addition of information relating to persons we haven't discussed being included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we ask, Mr. Lukic, may I take it that it's your intention that the Chamber looks at similar differences, and then sees whether those differences have any relevant because that's, I think what you tried to establish, that the -- I wouldn't even say inconsistencies but at least the different dates of disappearance or whatever, if there are any differences, that we look at that and consider for ourselves what those differences, also in relation to the persons we have not dealt with, what those mean for the entirety of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, it often happened that the Prosecution took a series of documents and said we have gone through three, four, or five and the rest is similar. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No objection to that exercise and if I can add, a number of these documents don't have a date, they don't have a heading, so in terms of provenance information perhaps if would be helpful for the witness -- to provide a little additional details on -- on where all these documents actually came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, for some of the type of the documents he has answered those questions. For some of the dates he was unable to give answers, but I leave it in Mr. Lukic's hands whether he wants to elicit more information, being aware now that for some of them it's set, and for some of them we have open questions. Mr. Jeremy, no objections. Mr. Registrar, therefore, the number -- the document is marked for identification, under seal, because it deals with individuals that should not be exposed to public eyes. And you'll tell us once the translation has been updated for those portions of the document which are not bilingual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Misic, we see -- actually, you have heard what my colleague, the Prosecutor, is concerned about regarding certain documents where we cannot see the date. There are some comments and there are some excerpts from the ICMP. How did the Defence obtain these documents?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the process of verification started, when I came to the position that I hold now, I tried to observe the rules and to look at the entire documentation before verifying the case of a particular person. And then the offices sent us documentation at our request, so these are documents that are from the institute. Since I cautioned institutions in Bosnia-Herzegovina several times and the co-founders, that is to say the ICMP, and the council of ministers, namely, that the process of verification is not evolving in accordance with what I spoke about yesterday. I looked at certain documents and I sent these documents asking the government of Republika Srpska as one of the co-founders of the institute or, rather, they gave agreement to have the institute established through the centre for studying war crimes, I sent these documents to them showing that something cannot be verified or considered to be verified until the procedure has been fully observed, that is to say the Law on Missing persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In several places in Bosnia-Herzegovina I submitted these documents and I tried to prove through these documents that something should be done from that level of government as well. I assume that you received this through the centre for investigating war crimes and some documents are absolutely known and some I have forgotten a bit, but I think that basically that would be that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness has talked about third of a page. The answer to your question is in the last sentence, and that answer is an assumption. The rest doesn't deal with the question you raised. You realise that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This documentation -- this document, Mr. Misic, could it be found in the institute for missing persons?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This entire documentation is from the institute. That is to say, it exists in the institute. Each and every one of these documents was received in the central records of missing persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The first question how the Defence obtained it is a question the Defence could answer itself. Mr. Lukic, tell us where you got it from as we often asked parties where does it come from how did you get.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We get it from the office for investigation of war crimes in Republika Srpska. I thought maybe the witness knows that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... But you know best.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He explained his step that he provided to that office. And we obtained it from that office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Who made the selection? I mean, you obtained it. Did you spontaneously get it or did you ask for it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It wasn't me who made the selection. We asked them to provide us with the files, with the documents they have in their possession. How many they have and how many they provided to us, I cannot tell you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was pretty open request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have much time left. Let us now take a look at 1D5448. We do not have a translation for these. These are guide-lines for the work of the commission for verifying information from the central records of missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The date is the 27th of May, 2010. Was this document in force when you came to the position that you hold today?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first version of these guide-lines and they were in force until I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 1D5447. While we're waiting for the document, could you just explain to us what was wrong with the document that is before us right now and what you did about it.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what it's all about. These guide-lines violated the rules and the law. That is to say, verification was carried out with less information than the minimum requirement according to law. And also it was carried out on the basis of documentation that is not referred to in the rules and the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have before us a cleared text, a final version for the guide-lines of the work of the commission of verification of information from the central records of the institute for missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do we have the same number 1D5447 in B/C/S in front of us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the two documents and the two versions as uploaded into e-court are as we see them on the screen. So apparently someone linked two documents which do not belong together. But perhaps we could see -- no, let's see. The -- the original document exists of six pages, whereas, the English version exists of only --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is different document. I can see both of them. It is completely different document on the right-hand side than English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then please -- we should have only the B/C/S on the screen and you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed on the basis and try to find the translation, Mr. Lukic, and then upload the right translation, attach it to this document. And I take it that the Prosecution will have a look at whether this document is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can my colleague leave the court so she can arrange that translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile, we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Misic, do tell us what you did and what was changed in this version as compared to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As briefly as possible, this is the version that ensures the minimum requirement as stipulated in the law. And also the records concerning missing persons that were kept in Bosnia-Herzegovina and that are being kept in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is to say, we should verify what we have in these records and that had not been done until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Part of these guide-lines, is it also a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILUTIN MISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The record of the commission and the conclusion are part of the work of the verification commission that is based on the following. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D5449 now.
